answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to post a refundable stake before trading, locked for a full epoch. Like a vine that only bears weight after it has grown, reputation accrues slowly: each completed job adds a small, non-transferable credit, and one proven fraud slashes both stake and history. An attacker spawning a plume of fake identities must fund every one and wait out the same slow growth, while honest agents keep timber-solid standing. Thousands of throwaway agents thus cost real capital and time, far more than one fraudulent deal can repay.
